ledger.note: 1246: Yaroslav Yaroslavich becomes the first prince of Tver. 'In 1246, another son of Yaroslav, Yaroslav Yaroslavich, became the first prince of Tver' and 'Tver became an independent principality when Yaroslav Yaroslavich was given the western slice of his father's patrimony' (infobox 'Established: 1246'); the Tver city page has Alexander Nevsky granting it to his younger brother in 1246. The page names the city and the Kashin-Zubtsov extent but gives no boundary or date for that extent.

region.text: Tver and the country round it, the part of the principality that Moscow's armies invaded in 1368 and 1370 and the Horde's punitive force sacked in 1327

ledger.note: 1327: the Horde, Moscow and Suzdal punish Tver's uprising. 'conflict broke out on August 15, 1327'; Ivan of Moscow 'was ordered to lead a punitive force, along with Alexander of Suzdal, to sack Tver' and 'received 50,000 Mongol warriors'; the army 'took dozens of captives and burned entire villages to the ground'. The page dates the uprising, not the expedition, so no month is given here.

region.text: Tver and the country round it, the part of the principality that Moscow's armies invaded in 1368 and 1370 and the Horde's punitive force sacked in 1327

ledger.note: 1327: the uprising is crushed and Tver stays a principality. The page is silent on the date the expedition ended; 'In 1328, Ozbeg divided the grand principality between Aleksandr of Suzdal and Ivan I of Moscow' and 'The uprising greatly reduced the Tver principality's power', with no land taken.

region.text: Tver and the country round it, the part of the principality that Moscow's armies invaded in 1368 and 1370 and the Horde's punitive force sacked in 1327

ledger.note: 1368: Moscow's army invades Tver. 'by 1368, the conflict had escalated when the Muscovite army invaded Tver' and 'Dmitry launched another invasion in 1370'; the Tver page has Tver siding 'with Lithuania against Moscow in the Lithuanian-Muscovite War of 1368-1372'. The page says 'by 1368', so the first campaign may be a little earlier.

region.text: Tver and the country round it, the part of the principality that Moscow's armies invaded in 1368 and 1370 and the Horde's punitive force sacked in 1327

ledger.note: 1375: Tver makes peace and calls Dmitry Donskoy 'elder brother'. 'The treaty recognized Dmitry Donskoy as "elder brother" and rightful grand prince of Vladimir' after a Muscovite-led expedition 'besieged Tver for four weeks'; the Moscow page adds that 'the combined forces defeated Mikhail's army' and that 'Mikhail once again received the patent in 1375'. Tver kept its land.

wars.name: Tver Uprising of 1327
wars.outcome: The uprising against Ozbeg's cousin Chol-khan was crushed by a Mongol force of 50,000 led by Ivan of Moscow and Alexander of Suzdal; Tver was burned and its power reduced, with no land taken.
wars.note: The Vladimir-Suzdal page names 'forces of Moscow and Nizhny Novgorod' as the helpers of the Mongols. The expedition is not dated beyond 1327, hence the zone is the contest_start/contest_end pair in the ledger and not a lasting border move.

wars.name: Struggle between Moscow and Tver for the grand princedom of Vladimir
wars.outcome: Moscow prevailed: Tver's princes held the Vladimir patent in 1305, 1322 and 1375 but Dmitry Donskoy's treaty of 1375 made Tver his junior ('elder brother').
wars.note: 'A struggle between the princes of Moscow and Tver began after Mikhail of Tver became grand prince in 1304'; 'Dmitry went to Sarai and received the patent for the grand princely title in 1322'; Mikhail 'once again received the patent in 1375'. The Tver page contradicts itself: 'In 1371, Mikhail II of Tver was the last prince of Tver ever appointed as the grand prince of Vladimir' and 'In 1375, Mamai again granted Mikhail II the yarlik'. Title only; no territory changed.

certainty.note: No page gives a treaty or survey line for Tver: 'Formerly a land of woods and bogs'; the Kashin and Zubtsov limits are approximate. The 1375 treaty and the 1470s treaties with Moscow fix the status of Tver, not a border.

notes: Page budget 5 (Principality of Tver, Tver, Tver Uprising of 1327, Principality of Moscow, Ivan III), all opened 2026-10-31. (1) Cliopatria's Tver shapes are all about 7,100 km2, a strip from Tver to Kashin, a quarter of the infobox's 28,450 km2; every shape is marked adjust with the page's Kashin-to-Zubtsov description as a union of three discs (about 32,000 km2 by the gazetteer). The page disagrees with itself: its prose puts the principality 'approximately in the area currently occupied by Tver Oblast and the eastern part of Smolensk Oblast' (Tver Oblast alone is 370 gazetteer cells, about 93,600 km2), its infobox gives 28,450 km2; I follow the infobox with the Kashin-Zubtsov limits, the lower reading. The infobox gives no year for the figure, and the page's extent is undated, so the same extent is applied to every year, with confidence 1 for the early years. (2) New keyframe tver_1246 fills 1246-1293, which Cliopatria lacks. (3) The seven Cliopatria shapes differ by under 2% from each other; the page gives no territorial change between 1246 and 1485, so there is no gain or loss event between the keyframes. The mid-14th-century appanages (Kashin, Kholm, Klin, Mikulin, Telyatyevo, Zubtsov) are undated and 'temporary'; not drawn as separate. (4) Cliopatria's Moscow shape holds all 32 cells of the Tver shape from 1482 although Tver fell on 12 September 1485: for the Moscow dossier. (5) Not settled: the Tver-Novgorod border (Torzhok), the Tver-Lithuania border to the west (Zubtsov, Rzhev) and the division into appanages after 1426 are not on the pages opened. The Tver page lists princes only in part (infobox 1247-1271 Yaroslav, 1461-1485 Mikhail III); no ruler strip is given. Gazetteer names needed: Kashin and Zubtsov (places), used as lon/lat discs. Counterparts: grand-principality-of-moscow, golden-horde, grand-duchy-of-lithuania, nizhny-novgorod have dossiers or will; principality-of-vladimir-suzdal is the later row of the predecessor state.
